'''''Ostrya carpinifolia''''', the '''European hop-hornbeam''', is a tree in the family [[Betulaceae]]. It is the only species of the genus ''[[Ostrya]]'' that is native to Europe.

The specific epithet ''carpinifolia'' means "hornbeam-leaved", from {{wikt-lang|la|carpinus}}, the Latin word for "[[hornbeam]]".

==Common name==
The name hophornbeam is derived from [[hops]], in reference to the shape of the tree's fruit, and the related [[hornbeam]] tree.

== Description ==
''Ostrya carpinifolia'' is a broadleaf deciduous tree, that can reach up to {{convert|21|m|ft}}.<ref name="Britannica">{{cite web |title=hop-hornbeam |url=https://www.britannica.com/plant/hop-hornbeam |website=Encyclopædia Britannica |access-date=6 May 2024 |language=en}}</ref>  It has a conical or irregular crown and a scaly, rough bark, and alternate and double-toothed birch-like leaves 3–10 cm long. The leaves are many-veined with 11-15 pairs and have a slightly hairy or smooth underside.<ref name="Václav">{{cite book |last1=Větvička |first1=Václav |title=The Illustrated Book of Trees & Shrubs |publisher=Octopus Books |editor1-last=Lawrence |editor1-first=Eleanor |isbn=0706420853 |page=143 |translator1-last=Kuthan |translator1-first=Ivan |translator2-last=Kuthanová |translator2-first=Vlasta |others=Illustrated by Mašek, Jan}}</ref>

The flowers are produced in spring, with male catkins {{convert|5|–|10|cm|in|0|abbr=on}} long and female catkins {{convert|2|–|5|cm|in|frac=4|abbr=on}} long. The fruit form in pendulous clusters {{convert|3|–|8|cm|in|frac=4|abbr=on}} long with 6–20 seeds; each seed is a small nut {{convert|2|–|4|mm|in|frac=16|abbr=on}} long, fully enclosed in a bladder-like involucre.

== Distribution and habitat ==
[[File:Ostrya carpinifolia MHNT.BOT.2004.0.156.jpg|thumb|Fruits of '' Ostrya carpinifolia'' – [[MHNT]]]]
''Ostrya carpinifolia'' is found in [[Lebanon]], [[Italy]], [[France]], [[Austria]], [[Slovenia]], [[Albania]], [[Croatia]], [[Bosnia and Herzegovina]], [[Serbia]], [[Montenegro]], [[North Macedonia]], [[Greece]], [[Bulgaria]], southern [[Switzerland]] and [[Turkey]]. It has been cultivated in [[England]] since before 1724.<ref name="Václav" />

In southern Italy and Sicily is found at medium elevations in the [[South Apennine mixed montane forests]] [[ecoregion]].

[[File:Ostrya carpinifolia legno.jpg|left|thumb|200px|The wood of Ostrya carpinifolia]]

== Uses ==
The wood is very heavy and hard, and was historically used to fashion plane soles. Other uses have included in the manufacture of wooden cogs and gears.<ref name="Václav" />

''Ostrya'' are used as food plants by the larvae of some [[Lepidoptera]] species.
